slides.title: MSS Colorectal Cancer: The Last Major Solid Tumor Without Immunotherapy

content.headline: ~85% of metastatic CRC is MSS/pMMR — and has no approved immunotherapy

items.label: new metastatic CRC cases/year in the US
are MSS/pMMR — immune checkpoint inhibitors do not work
items.source: Le et al. NEJM 2015; NCCN guidelines

items.label: MSS mCRC patients/year in the US with no immunotherapy option
objective response rate with current 2L standard of care

columns.header: Why Checkpoint Inhibitors Fail in MSS CRC
items: Low tumor mutational burden (TMB) → few neoantigens → T cells not primed
Immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TGF-β, SMAD4 loss, myeloid suppression)
CEACAM5 overexpression sequesters tumor antigens at intercellular junctions
MSS tumors are 'cold' — immune cells cannot infiltrate
Pembrolizumab approved only for MSI-H/dMMR CRC (~15% of cases) — the MSS majority is excluded

content.footnote: MSS = microsatellite stable; pMMR = proficient mismatch repair; dMMR = deficient mismatch repair; MSI-H = microsatellite instability-high.

slides.speaker_notes: The unmet need is large and well-defined. ~46,750 MSS mCRC patients per year in the US have no approved immunotherapy. Checkpoint inhibitors (pembrolizumab, nivolumab) are approved only for the MSI-H/dMMR minority (~15%). The MSS majority — 85% of cases — is excluded. Current 2L standard of care (FOLFIRI ± bevacizumab) produces ORR ~5–7%. The biology of MSS CRC explains why: low TMB, immunosuppressive TME, and antigen sequestration all prevent immune activation. Brenus's approach is to bypass these barriers by educating the immune system ex vivo before re-exposing it to the tumor.

slides.title: The Biology: Why MSS CRC Needs a Different Approach
slides.subtitle: Three barriers that block conventional immunotherapy — and how STC-1010 addresses each

bullets.problem: MSS CRC tumors express low levels of neoantigens. T cells are never primed against the tumor.
bullets.stc_solution: STC-1010 presents >200 tumor-associated and tumor-specific antigens simultaneously — including CEACAM5, MUC1, and CEA — to educate the immune system against the full tumor antigen landscape.

bullets.problem: The MSS CRC tumor microenvironment is immunosuppressive: TGF-β signaling, SMAD4 loss (~30% of MSS CRC), and myeloid cell infiltration prevent T cell activity.
bullets.stc_solution: STC-1010 is combined with low-dose cyclophosphamide (regulatory T cell depletion) and GM-CSF (dendritic cell activation) to overcome suppression before tumor re-exposure.

bullets.problem: MSS CRC tumors lack tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs). Even if T cells are primed, they cannot enter the tumor.
bullets.stc_solution: Haptenization with DNFB creates a contact hypersensitivity response that recruits immune cells to the tumor site — converting a 'cold' tumor to an 'inflamed' state.
bullets.source: Alzeeb et al. 2024; AACR IO 2026 press release (Feb 19, 2026)

content.footnote: CEACAM5 = carcinoembryonic antigen-related cell adhesion molecule 5; DNFB = dinitrofluorobenzene; TGF-β = transforming growth factor beta; SMAD4 = mothers against decapentaplegic homolog 4.

slides.speaker_notes: Three barriers explain why checkpoint inhibitors fail in MSS CRC and why a vaccine approach is rational. First, antigen invisibility: MSS tumors have low TMB, so T cells are never primed. STC-1010 bypasses this by presenting >200 antigens directly to dendritic cells. Second, immune suppression: TGF-β and regulatory T cells prevent effector T cell activity. The combination regimen (cyclophosphamide + GM-CSF) addresses this pharmacologically. Third, cold TME: even primed T cells cannot enter MSS tumors. DNFB haptenization creates a contact hypersensitivity response that recruits immune cells to the tumor site. Each barrier has a specific mechanistic counter in the STC-1010 regimen.

slides.title: The STC Platform: Stimulated Tumor Cell Technology
slides.subtitle: An off-the-shelf, allogeneic, in vivo immunotherapy that educates the immune system against the full tumor antigen landscape

items.label: Starting material
items.value: Established human CRC cell lines (HCT116, HT29, LoVo) — provisional, high confidence

items.label: Stress induction
items.value: Controlled physical (irradiation, heat shock) or chemical (chemotherapy) stress → overexpression of tumor-associated and tumor-specific antigens

items.label: Haptenization
items.value: DNFB (dinitrofluorobenzene) conjugated to stressed cells → contact hypersensitivity signal that recruits immune cells to tumor

items.label: Final product
items.value: Non-proliferative 'ghost cells' presenting >200 tumor antigens in an immunogenic context

items.detail: Targets >200 tumor antigens simultaneously — not a single-antigen approach. Resistant to antigen escape.
Allogeneic — no patient-specific manufacturing. Standardized production process. Company claims ~100 patients treatable per batch (unvalidated independently).
Designed to combine with SOC chemotherapy (mFOLFOX6 ± bevacizumab) — not a standalone therapy. Chemotherapy-induced immunogenic cell death amplifies the vaccine signal.
DNFB haptenization is a validated contact hypersensitivity mechanism (used in dermatology for decades). Applied here to recruit immune cells to the tumor site.
Platform applicable to any solid tumor expressing the target antigen panel. CRC is the lead indication; gastric and pancreatic cancer are aspirational extensions.

content.footnote: Cell line identity (HCT116, HT29, LoVo) is provisional — high confidence based on ASCO 2023 abstract e14661, EACR25 abstract, and Brenus platform page; full confirmation requires NDA data room access. HT29 carries BRAF V600E — potential conflict with trial BRAF-exclusion criterion (NCT06934538 Exclusion Criterion #7). '>200 tumor antigens' is a company claim; Alzeeb et al. 2024 reports 1,196+ proteins by MS but does not enumerate 200+ validated targets.

slides.speaker_notes: The STC platform is the core IP. The key insight is that stressed tumor cells — cells that have been irradiated or chemotherapy-treated — overexpress a broad panel of tumor antigens in a highly immunogenic context. Haptenization with DNFB adds a contact hypersensitivity signal that recruits immune cells to the tumor site. The result is a non-proliferative 'ghost cell' that presents >200 antigens to the immune system. The off-the-shelf format is a major commercial advantage: no patient-specific manufacturing, standardized batches, and scalable production. The combination with mFOLFOX6 is intentional: chemotherapy-induced immunogenic cell death releases additional tumor antigens that amplify the vaccine signal.

slides.title: How STC-1010 Works: A Four-Step Immune Education Process

content.headline: STC-1010 converts a 'cold' MSS CRC tumor into an immune-recognized target through four sequential steps

bullets.detail: Allogeneic CRC cell lines are subjected to controlled stress (irradiation or chemotherapy). Stress induces overexpression of tumor-associated antigens (TAA) and tumor-specific antigens (TSA). Cells are haptenized with DNFB and rendered non-proliferative ('ghost cells'). Standardized batches produced under GMP.
bullets.evidence: Alzeeb et al. 2024; AACR 2024 abstract 5003 (batch reproducibility confirmed)

bullets.detail: STC-1010 is administered with low-dose cyclophosphamide (depletes regulatory T cells) and GM-CSF (activates dendritic cells). Dendritic cells capture STC-1010, process antigens, and prime CD8+ cytotoxic T cells against the tumor antigen panel.
bullets.evidence: NCT06934538 protocol; AACR 2025 LB383 (DC activation, CD8+ T cell priming confirmed ex vivo)

bullets.detail: DNFB haptenization creates a contact hypersensitivity (DTH) response at the tumor site. Immune cells are recruited to the tumor microenvironment. DTH responses observed in first-in-human patients (AACR 2026, n=6).
bullets.evidence: AACR 2026 press release (Apr 14, 2026); AACR IO 2026 press release (Feb 19, 2026)

bullets.detail: Primed CD8+ T cells kill CEACAM5+ and neighboring tumor cells (bystander effect). Concurrent mFOLFOX6 chemotherapy induces immunogenic cell death, releasing additional tumor antigens that amplify the vaccine signal in a feed-forward loop.
bullets.evidence: Alzeeb et al. 2024; AACR 2025 LB383 (robust, reproducible cytotoxicity confirmed ex vivo)

content.footnote: Steps 1–2 are confirmed in preclinical models and ex vivo. Step 3 (DTH) is confirmed in first-in-human data (n=6, AACR 2026). Step 4 (tumor killing in humans) is the primary endpoint of Phase IIa — data expected 2027–2028.

slides.speaker_notes: The four-step mechanism is important for the CMO audience. Step 1 is manufacturing — the off-the-shelf advantage. Step 2 is immune priming — the combination regimen is not arbitrary; each component has a specific role. Step 3 is the DNFB mechanism — this is the most novel part of the platform. Contact hypersensitivity is a well-understood dermatology mechanism being applied to oncology. DTH responses have been observed in the first 6 FIH patients — this is the first human evidence that the mechanism is working as designed. Step 4 is the efficacy endpoint — not yet confirmed in humans. The 100% DCR in n=6 patients is encouraging but must be interpreted with caution: DCR includes stable disease, n=6 is very small, and there is no comparator arm.

content.footnote: All clinical data are from company press releases. No peer-reviewed clinical publication exists as of June 2026. n=6 is insufficient to draw efficacy conclusions. The 100% DCR must be interpreted in the context of FOLFOX backbone (expected DCR ~80–90% in 1L mCRC). The primary efficacy endpoint (12-month non-progression rate) will be measured in Phase IIa — data expected 2027–2028.

slides.speaker_notes: The FIH data is early but meaningful. The most important finding is safety: no DLTs across all first dose levels. This clears the path to Phase IIa. The 100% DCR is encouraging but must be contextualized: FOLFOX alone produces ~80–90% DCR in 1L mCRC, so the incremental contribution of STC-1010 cannot be assessed from this data. The DTH responses are the most scientifically interesting finding: they confirm that the DNFB mechanism is working in humans — immune cells are being recruited to the tumor site. This is the first human evidence that the platform's core mechanism is functioning as designed. Full Phase Ia data (all dose cohorts) expected Q2 2026. Phase IIa (12-month non-progression rate as primary endpoint) will provide the first efficacy readout.

slides.title: Why Now: The Convergence of Unmet Need, Platform Readiness, and Competitive Window

content.headline: Three reasons the timing is right

bullets.reason: 1. The unmet need is large and unaddressed
bullets.detail: ~46,750 MSS mCRC patients per year in the US have no approved immunotherapy. Current 2L standard of care produces ~5–7% ORR. No competitor has a validated patient selection system for this population. Checkpoint inhibitors are approved only for the MSI-H minority (~15% of CRC).

bullets.reason: 2. The platform is de-risked at the critical safety gate
bullets.detail: No DLTs across all Phase Ia dose levels (n=6, 6-month follow-up). DTH responses confirmed in humans — the core DNFB mechanism is working as designed. Batch reproducibility confirmed across 3 GMP batches. Full Phase Ia data (all dose cohorts) expected Q2 2026.

bullets.reason: 3. The competitive window is open — but not indefinitely
bullets.detail: No approved immunotherapy for MSS CRC. Competing programs (SGN-CEACAM5C, M9140) are enrolling without validated patient selection — the same approach that failed in CARMEN-LC03. Brenus's combination of broad antigen targeting, hapten-mediated immune recruitment, and first-line positioning is differentiated from all current competitors.
bullets.evidence_label: SOURCED for competitive landscape; OPEN_ASSUMPTION for competitive advantage claim

ask.label: The Ask
items: Phase IIa partnership / co-development in MSS CRC
Biomarker collaboration: patient selection platform development (CrisPRO fit)
US IND support and Johns Hopkins site activation
Strategic licensing: STC platform for gastric / pancreatic extensions (aspirational)

content.footnote: Competitive landscape claims are based on publicly available trial registry data (NCT06131840 for SGN-CEACAM5C). CARMEN-LC03 failure data: Besse et al. WCLC 2024. The 'competitive advantage' framing is a strategic interpretation, not a sourced claim.

slides.speaker_notes: The closing slide makes three arguments: unmet need, platform readiness, and competitive window. The unmet need is the largest and most defensible: 46,750 patients per year with no immunotherapy option. Platform readiness: the safety gate has been cleared. No DLTs is the minimum required to proceed to Phase IIa. DTH responses are the first human evidence that the mechanism is working. Competitive window: no competitor has a validated patient selection system for MSS CRC. The CARMEN-LC03 failure (Sanofi/tusamitamab) demonstrates that broad enrollment without biomarker selection fails. Brenus's first-line positioning and broad antigen targeting differentiate it from ADC-based approaches. The ask is deliberately staged: Phase IIa partnership is the entry point; biomarker collaboration (CrisPRO) is the value-add; US expansion is the growth path.
